guidance.heading: Fiscal 2027 Outlook
section: • | Maintains 7 to 9 percent long-term NFEPS growth target, starting from a fiscal 2025 base of $2.83 per share**
• | Introduces fiscal 2027 NFEPS guidance range of $3.25 to $3.40

desk.headline: Q4 NFEPS fell to $0.11, a miss, though revenue rose 11% to $374.4m and beat; fiscal 2027 guidance of $3.25–3.40 set, below FY26's $3.58

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (net financial earnings per basic share)

results: Fourth-quarter net financial earnings (NFE, the company's adjusted profit) fell to $10.7m, or $0.11 a share, from $0.16; GAAP EPS rose to $0.17 from $0.15.
The quarter's drop came mainly from the gas utility, whose seasonal summer loss widened to $24.4m on higher depreciation and interest costs.
Full year NFEPS rose to $3.58 from $3.29, lifted by Energy Services, whose NFE more than doubled to $76.7m thanks to winter gas price swings; storage and pipelines NFE rose to $33.4m from $18.5m.
Solar NFE fell to $37.6m from $61.2m because last year included a gain on selling the residential solar business; 72.4 MW of new commercial solar took capacity to about 552 MW.
Operating cash flow rose to $641.2m; capital spending was $734.3m. The utility cut average customer bills by 9% (about $158 a year) from 1 October.

guidance.summary: NJR set its first fiscal 2027 range: NFEPS of $3.25–3.40, below the $3.58 earned in fiscal 2026, when Energy Services had an unusually strong winter. It kept its 7–9% long-term NFEPS growth target from a $2.83 fiscal 2025 base and plans $5.3–5.7bn of capital spending over fiscal 2027–2031.

points: The call slides stress a sixth straight year of beating initial guidance: FY26 NFEPS of $3.58 was about $0.45 above the original midpoint.
Growth is to be funded without a large share sale ("no block equity"), with adjusted funds from operations to debt averaging 20–21% through FY2031.
Storage and transport NFE is expected to double from FY2025 to FY2027 on better contracts and reach $55–65m by FY2029, with Leaf River storage expanding to 55.2 Bcf by 2031.
The utility targets 630–640K customers by FY2031 (596K now) and has a pending base rate case seeking about $158.3m a year.
The solar unit cites its largest-ever project pipeline, about $2.15bn of tax-credit-eligible projects.
call.source: Investor presentation for the 19 Nov 2026 call (Exhibit 99.2); no news coverage of the call itself found

watch: The outcome of the NJNG base rate case (about $158.3m a year requested, 10.10% return on equity).
How much Energy Services earns this winter, given guidance assumes a smaller share than in fiscal 2026.
Progress on the Leaf River storage expansion and new solar projects coming into service.
